Welcome to Ann Edwards Church of England Primary School
Learning and achieving in a caring community
“Do to others what you would want them to do to you.” – Matthew 7:12
Our special chosen Bible story is the Parable of The Good Samaritan.
Please click here to read our SIAMS inspection report (October 2023) and here to read our OFSTED report
Welcome to Ann Edwards Church of England Primary School, in the lovely Cotswold village of South Cerney.
Our School Vision is ‘Learning and Achieving in a Caring Community’ and this shines through in everything we do. I am proud of our vibrant, child-centred and inclusive school, including the approachable, skilled and hard-working staff, our amazing children and our supportive community, including the fantastic PTA.
Our spacious building includes a library, sensory room, music room and nurture room, a designated space for wraparound care and a large indoor and outdoor space for our Reception children. We also enjoy extensive grounds which include a Forest School site, adventure playground and a large field for all the children to learn and play.
I hope you find our website a useful source of information about our school’s values, organisation and curriculum. Although we communicate and celebrate with our parents using the internal Class Dojo platform, you can access the latest half-termly newsletters on our website and find out other information in the News section.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Ann Edwards Church of England Primary School
Learning and achieving in a caring community
“Do to others what you would want them to do to you.” – Matthew 7:12
Our special chosen Bible story is the Parable of The Good Samaritan.
Please click here to read our SIAMS inspection report (October 2023) and here to read our OFSTED report
Welcome to Ann Edwards Church of England Primary School, in the lovely Cotswold village of South Cerney.
Our School Vision is ‘Learning and Achieving in a Caring Community’ and this shines through in everything we do. I am proud of our vibrant, child-centred and inclusive school, including the approachable, skilled and hard-working staff, our amazing children and our supportive community, including the fantastic PTA.
Our spacious building includes a library, sensory room, music room and nurture room, a designated space for wraparound care and a large indoor and outdoor space for our Reception children. We also enjoy extensive grounds which include a Forest School site, adventure playground and a large field for all the children to learn and play.
I hope you find our website a useful source of information about our school’s values, organisation and curriculum. Although we communicate and celebrate with our parents using the internal Class Dojo platform, you can access the latest half-termly newsletters on our website and find out other information in the News section.
We are a Voluntary Controlled Church of England Primary School that caters for boys and girls aged 4 to 11. We have approximately 205 children on roll, in eight classes.
Our curriculum extends beyond the National Curriculum to nurture our children, install secure values, stoke their curiosity, aid their spiritual growth and enable them to serve as responsible 21st century citizens. Our teachers are trained in Philosophy for Children, we have two Emotional Literacy Support Assistants (ELSAs) and all staff have completed trauma-informed schools training, phonics training and much more.
Strong links are maintained with the communities we serve and with our local church, All Hallows. Our Christian ethos provides a spiritual and moral context that helps children to grow into thinking, caring people. We are supported in this by the Diocese of Gloucester, and I am a trustee for their Board of Education.
Children come to our school from South Cerney, Cerney Wick, Somerford Keynes, other neighbouring villages and from Cirencester. We also take children from the 29th Regiment RLC and Four Acres Caravan Park. Our main feeder playgroups are South Cerney Playgroup and the Duke of Gloucester Playgroup.
We work in partnership with parents and carers to ensure that children make the very best of their time at Ann Edwards School, so that they look back on their primary schooldays with pleasure.
‘Childhood is for life’ – Floella Benjamin

pageCache.pageTitle: Science – Ann Edwards CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Science
“The important thing in science is not so much to obtain new facts as to discover new ways of thinking about them.” – William Lawrence Bragg
Science Intent
Our Science lessons are practical, creative and engage children through regularly seeking out and making the most of awe and wonder in the world, developing a long-lasting love of science. Through regular elicitation, we allow the children space and time to explore and address misconceptions, immerse themselves into key scientific topics and we place a high importance on appreciating, respecting and protecting the natural environment. Our sequenced Science provision is accessible, yet ambitious for all, where topics, such as plants, are taught across both key stages to build upon prior knowledge, whilst simultaneously developing the children’s scientific skills and lines of enquiry across Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Science is linked with other subjects throughout the curriculum, including Geography, Maths and English, which embeds the learning into the children’s long-term memory. We draw upon the children’s natural curiosity to deliver a vibrant and innovative Science curriculum as well as incorporating experiences to develop cultural capital through learning outside the curriculum, with STEM opportunities, involving our link with INTEL, Forest School and inspirational visitors and trips.
Aims
The overarching aim for Science in our school is to ensure that pupils:
To develop scientific knowledge and understanding
To develop scientific enquiry skills
To work safely

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum – Ann Edwards CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Curriculum Intent
Our vibrant, creative curriculum puts the children at the forefront of the educational experience, inspiring a lifelong love of, and achievement in, learning, reading and thinking. Our ‘beginning with a hook’ approach leads into engaging, exciting and relevant lessons that make education an enjoyable experience through which our pupils then grow in the key areas of Caring, Collaboration, Creativity and Critical Thinking. Our skilled, aspirational and committed team endeavours to nurture our pupils’ unique academic and emotional needs, supporting them in fulfilling their ambitions regardless of background, special educational needs or disability. We have high aspirations for learning, seeking academic excellence, through encouraging all of our pupils to achieve well and make strong progress in order to be ready for each next stage of their education.
We believe not only that a safe, engaged and resilient student is a good learner, but that happiness and mental and physical wellbeing should be ends to themselves. Ann Edwards Church of England Primary School provides a warm, calm and caring environment that promotes confidence, kindness, inquiry, mutual support and respect while helping pupils to develop resilience and self-discipline. We are passionate about empowering our children by giving them the skills and confidence to communicate well and explore their thoughts and feelings, as well as giving them rich opportunities to creatively express themselves.
As a Church school, we live out our vision of ‘Learning and achieving in a caring community’ in everything we do, offering guidance through the teachings of Christ and moments of calm, stillness and reflection. We live out our vision, deliver our curriculum intent, teach and promote our seven core values of Respect, Service, Perseverance, Forgiveness, Compassion, Creativity and Thankfulness in accordance with the LIFE Together Vision of the Diocese of Gloucester which seeks to enable Life in All Its Fullness (John 10:10), through Leadership, Imagination, Faith and Engagement. Our pupils are taught to embrace their own beliefs and be respectful of the beliefs, customs and practices of others. Our children develop a strong sense of belonging to our school and local communities as well as being equipped to make a positive contribution to the wider world, including understanding their impact on the environment and improving sustainability.

pageCache.pageTitle: English – Ann Edwards CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
English
“The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.” Ludwig Wittgenstein (philosopher)
English Intent
At Ann Edwards we are passionate about empowering our children by giving them the skills, knowledge and confidence to communicate their thoughts and feelings, as well as having the opportunity to creatively express themselves. We precision teach systematic synthetic phonics, currently using Letters and Sounds (transitioning to Phonics Bug), beginning with our youngest pupils and extending across the whole school. Research continues to show that robust phonics teaching will lay solid foundations for pupils to build towards becoming fluent, confident and competent readers and we place it at the heart of our learning progression. Once acquired, children can begin to develop other areas of their reading, such as comprehension, which they are taught specifically through carefully sequenced guided reading sessions and targeted interventions, where appropriate.
We are committed to embedding oracy within and across all subjects and seek to underpin our curriculum with the teaching of four fundamental strands of oracy: physical, linguistic, cognitive, social and emotional. With oracy at the centre of our children’s learning, they will gain the skills they will need to become effective speakers and listeners, helping them to not only understand themselves, but the wider world around them.
With this in mind, an overarching focal point, for us as a school, is our endeavour to close the vocabulary gap within and across year groups. We strive to achieve this through focussed vocabulary teaching and providing time for the children to embed the language they have learnt. Inspired by acclaimed literature, our three part, whole-school writing process – with oracy at its core – allows our dedicated team to ensure lessons are innovative, fun and purposeful for all learners. It is important to us that our pupils achieve their full potential and are prepared for the next stage of their education. We help our pupils communicate their thoughts, ideas and emotions in a clear and healthy way, whilst also creating a life-long love and appreciation of language, reading and writing.
The national curriculum for English aims to ensure that all pupils:
read easily, fluently and with good understanding
acquire a wide vocabulary,
Writing and Spoken Language
appreciate our rich and varied literary heritage

pageCache.pageTitle: Mathematics – Ann Edwards CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
“Pure mathematics is, in its way, the poetry of logical ideas.”
– Albert Einstein, German theoretical physicist
Maths Intent
At the heart of our innovative and inclusive Mathematics curriculum is facilitating opportunities for children to develop skills and knowledge which places a focus on perceiving how Maths surrounds their everyday lives. Putting children at the forefront of their learning is paramount to providing a 21st century education, ready for their next steps. Through fluency of fundamental skills, reasoning of key concepts and making connections in problem solving, children are taught to detect patterns, explain their thinking using mathematical vocabulary, think logically and respect others’ approaches when exploring different mathematical concepts. As well as independent work, a range of paired, group and whole class activities allow children to build upon their knowledge and understanding and support others in their learning.
By the time the children reach Year 6, they will have been exposed to high standards of subject-specific vocabulary and will be competent in mathematical oracy. Embedded within our Mathematics provision, which we aim to instil, are core values of resilience, perseverance and determination, key values that are not standalone; they allow children to flourish in real-life situations.
The Maths National Curriculum aims to ensure all pupils:
Maths at Ann Edwards
In order to further develop children’s understanding of Maths, our approach to teaching Mathematics increases the depth in which we were covering Maths, instead of purely teaching Mathematical skills. We want children to develop a greater conceptual understanding of Maths and where it can be used. Objectives from the National Curriculum are broken down into manageable steps, taken from the CanDo Maths Scheme. We have Road Maps for each year group mapping out the mathematical units taught throughout the year.
Our approach is a three-step system which allows all children, regardless of confidence in Maths, to access all key mathematical skills. The three-steps are ‘Do it’ (mild), ‘Secure it’ (Hot) and ‘Deepen it’ (Spicy). The children are able to work their way through each activity, as outlined below.
In EYFS and Year 1, the maths activities are recorded in a floor book.
Year 1 move to working in maths books when appropriate, during term 1 or term 2.
Children begin with an activity that consists of questions which allow practise of the overall skill that the children are being taught. These questions come in different forms as it is important for children to be able to connect mathematical concepts to even the most abstract situations. This is also in preparation for statutory assessments that the children sit at the end of Key Stage 2 (Year 6).
Once ‘Do it’ has been completed, the children move onto the ‘Secure it’ activity. This will present the children with 1 question, where they need to use the skills they have learnt in order to reason. An example of a reasoning question would be to challenge either a statement or answer presented to them, which provides an idea or theory about a mathematical concept. We use a DNA approach for children to explain their answer. D – do it (answer the question), N – what do you notice?, A – what advice do you give?
The final activity is usually a problem solving activity which challenges the children to apply their understanding of mathematical concepts where there are often multiple solutions to a problem. This is also an opportunity for children to put into practice the British and school values that we promote at Ann Edwards Primary School, e.g. perseverance and resilience.
We place a big focus on vocabulary here at Ann Edwards Primary School across all subjects. Specifically in Maths, it is crucial that the children are exposed to and aware of subject specific vocabulary as this is key to understanding mathematical concepts. Children are expected to use their learnt mathematical vocabulary in lessons on a regular basis, particularly when reasoning, both verbally and in written format. At the start of each unit, the key vocabulary is stuck in to maths books allowing the children to refer to these during their learning. The key vocabulary is then revisited at the start of each lesson and displayed on our working walls.
We understand how how important it is to develop key arithmetic skills. Year 1 to Year 6 have a daily arithmetic session, which is separate from the Maths lesson. They last 10 to 15 minute sessions and revisit previous learning or are used to pre-teach a skill. The work may be practical, completed on whiteboards or recorded in books.
We also have daily fluency activities, which take place daily for 10 minutes. The aim is to develop rapid recall of key facts. Teacher’s plan an activity covering the objectives from our progression in instant recall facts document. Teacher’s can plan an activity to recap an objective from a previous year group, when needed.
The activity can be a whole class game, an on-line game, a set of calculations etc.
